headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if Copilot consumes OpenMetadata MCP/API outputs; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server. That creates a plausible bridge where OpenMetadata content can reach Copilot as trusted text. The pair is not documented as directly integrated, so uncertainty remains, but the interaction is credible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is pasted or synced into Copilot-visible buffers, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Copilot Workspace ingests OpenMetadata-generated text without provenance filtering, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata outputs into Copilot-visible files.
Require provenance labels on any OpenMetadata text before Copilot reads it.
Use a manual review step for all generated instructions.
Restrict OpenMetadata MCP/webhook payloads to structured fields only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data through APIs and MCP. If those data classes are placed into shared buffers or prompts, they can flow to a third-party backend. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF governance or lineage records are copied into Copilot editor buffers, they may be transmitted to GitHub's backend.
IF OpenMetadata MCP responses include sensitive metadata and are fed into Copilot prompts, leakage is possible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive OpenMetadata records out of Copilot-visible buffers.
Redact governance and lineage fields before any prompt construction.
Use separate accounts and workspaces for the two tools.
Review outbound Copilot prompts for sensitive metadata.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP but no explicit filesystem write capability is listed. The overlap is therefore limited and not enough to show a same-directory write conflict. Because OpenMetadata's write surface is underspecified, uncertainty is resolved upward only to low, not none.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata is configured to mutate the same repository through an API-backed workflow, write contention can appear.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while OpenMetadata also updates the same artifacts, conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo path.
Serialize changes through one operator at a time.
Use branch-based workflows for Copilot edits.
Pause OpenMetadata write workflows during Copilot Workspace sessions.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces completions and Workspace edits for human review, while OpenMetadata can emit metadata through APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If OpenMetadata output is treated as authoritative input to Copilot, errors can cascade into generated code or metadata actions. The human-review step lowers severity below high, but the pathway still exists in default usage patterns.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhook or MCP output is fed into Copilot prompts without verification, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Copilot Workspace edits are accepted without human review, incorrect metadata-driven changes can be applied.
mitigations: Require verification before Copilot consumes OpenMetadata output.
Keep human review enabled for all Workspace edits.
Add schema checks to OpenMetadata-derived inputs.
Limit Copilot to suggestion mode for metadata-sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: implement validation gates between metadata and code-generation steps.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo OAuth scope and vendor-only egress, while OpenMetadata is open-source and can process governance and lineage data through APIs and MCP. If regulated metadata or residency-bound records are routed into Copilot, compliance obligations may differ across the pair. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated governance or lineage data is sent from OpenMetadata into Copilot prompts, policy mismatch may occur.
IF the deployment requires residency controls that Copilot's vendor-only egress cannot satisfy, compliance risk materializes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot prompts.
Document which data classes may cross from OpenMetadata to Copilot.
Review vendor and residency terms before enabling integration.
Use separate retention policies for each tool.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and residency routing controls.
